sentences.text: A retrospective study examined 96 patients who received repeat stereotactic radiosurgery for recurrent brain metastases between 2016 and 2025.

Those receiving a second radiation course showed a 78.7% local control rate at 12 months with a median progression-free time of 47.1 months, while radiological signs of damage appeared in 40.9% of cases and symptoms in 14.6%, all of which improved after corticosteroid treatment.
No deaths were directly caused by the treatment, though the authors conclude that future forward-looking studies are required to better select patients and predict risks.
